{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wy-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"5c2d8f109e48070484bd6f416b011bd84cdfef59449025b6afec6adbfba05616","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wy-class-c:lineage:19","source_registry_sha256":"f2806994ac56e29c3588fb4e8e2cc870c5f64d0616933994765d31d7841ccbe9","source_liveness_sha256":"e9e98c5695424e30c400f1e14b2593178d09ca723f8f00581c9655dcae32ca6c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Safety belts and child restraints — C.01","heading":"C — Safety belts and child restraints","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Safety belts and child restraints
FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
The handbook's general safety-belt rule covers every vehicle occupant, including the driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
The driver is responsible for seeing that occupants comply with the safety-belt law. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Children must be secured properly in an appropriate child-restraint system. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
The lap belt should fit snugly over the hip bones. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A01
The lap belt should never rest over the stomach or soft abdomen. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A01
The shoulder belt should allow enough movement for the driver to reach important controls. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A01
The shoulder belt should not be used by itself. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A02
The child-restraint guide covers children who have not yet turned nine. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A02
The child-restraint guide applies to every driver operating a privately owned, leased or rented noncommercial passenger vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A02
The child-restraint requirements apply to residents and nonresidents alike. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A02
A child covered by the guide must use a seat other than the front, except in a single-row vehicle or when other child passengers are using all safety belts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A02
A rear-facing infant restraint must never be placed in front of an active airbag. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A02
The child must be secured in the restraint according to the manufacturer's instructions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A02
The child restraint must also be installed according to the manufacturer's instructions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A02
A child restraint must meet Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 213. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A02
Nonuse or misuse of a child restraint is a primary offense that provides reasonable suspicion to stop a vehicle and investigate a suspected violation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A02
The maximum fine for a first child-restraint offense is $60. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A02
The court must waive the first-offense fine when it receives proof that an approved restraint was purchased, leased or otherwise acquired after the offense. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A02
The maximum fine for a second or later child-restraint offense is $110. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A02
A child within the covered age range is exempt from a separate child restraint when the lap and shoulder belt fits the collarbone, chest and hips properly without endangering the neck, face or abdomen during a crash or sudden stop. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A02
The medical child-restraint exemption requires a signed physician statement kept in the car saying that the child should not use a child-restraint system. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A02
A vehicle not equipped with safety belts when manufactured is exempt from the child-restraint requirements. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A02
The guide identifies passenger vehicles before model year 1967 and vans or trucks before model year 1972 in its exemption for vehicles manufactured without safety belts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A02
Emergency vehicles and law-enforcement vehicles are exempt from the child-restraint requirements. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A02
The child-restraint exemption list includes school buses, including private or church buses, when used to transport children. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A02
The exemption list also includes public-transportation buses or other public-transportation vehicles manufactured without seat belts. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A02
The child-restraint exemption list covers a driver rendering aid or assistance to the child, parent or guardian. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0030]

Misconceptions: General belt exemptions and child-restraint exemptions are separate lists; a booster recommendation does not erase the child-restraint law's conditions.
Mnemonics: Recall index: scope, placement, fit, exemption; this is an authored organizer rather than an added legal rule.
Glossary: Recall terms: lap belt, shoulder belt, rear-facing restraint, belt-positioning booster and primary offense.
Dynamic facts: Contact numbers and service locations are withheld. Legal penalties and restraint rules remain edition-bound and require current applicability review.
